# Gemba

> The agent-runtime platform. Stand up the environment, run agent sessions,
> read the traces, keep the memory, measure the outcomes, and stop the team
> when it runs away. Six commands and five CI actions run one loop.

Gemba is the platform a team hires to run coding agents continuously. In Lean
practice, gemba is the factory floor, the place where value gets made. This
platform is that floor for an agent team. The loop is stand up, run, see,
remember, measure, and stop. The platform ships that loop twice. It ships a
command family for a terminal and composite actions for GitHub Actions. What a
team rehearses locally is what runs on every push. Kata is the reference
tenant. It runs this platform every day, and it is a separate product with its
own site at https://www.kata.team/.

Six commands cover the loop. `gemba-harness` runs single-agent and multi-agent
sessions and captures one NDJSON trace. `gemba-trace` queries those traces for
turns, tool calls, errors, and token cost. `gemba-wiki` keeps persistent
memory as boot digests, claims, memos, and integrity audits. `gemba-xmr`
charts a metric as an XmR control chart, so the team acts on signal instead of
noise. `gemba-benchmark` grades a task family across repeated runs with hidden
tests and reports pass@k. `gemba-watchdog` counts repository activity over
a window and engages an operator latch variable when a counter breaches its
threshold.

Five published composite actions run the same loop in CI. `gemba-bootstrap`
installs the pinned toolchain and the platform CLIs. `gemba-harness` runs an
agent task and uploads the trace. `gemba-wiki` runs a memory command with a
freshly minted token. `gemba-benchmark` runs benchmark families across
machines and merges the reports. `gemba-watchdog` counts repository activity
and engages the latch on a breach. A workflow pins each action by SHA.

Install the skill pack with `apm install forwardimpact/gemba-skills`, then ask
Claude to stand up the team. For the commands alone, run
`npm install -g @forwardimpact/gemba`.
